title.analysis: Authentic title "Average 401K Balance By Age - 2026 Edition!" is a search-style benchmark query with a year tag. The script turns the query against itself: it argues the average is a "Phantom Saver", gives medians by age, then shifts to coverage gaps, leakage, defaults and two-tier Roth outcomes. TYPICAL against the cohort. Association only.

script.opening_words: It's 11:40 on a Tuesday night and Jem is standing at her kitchen counter in a hospital badge she forgot to take off eating cereal out of a coffee mug because the bowls are in the dishwasher. She's 41. Open behind her search bar is a tab from 3 hours ago where she was pricing a water heater. She types average 401k balance by age, reads the number for her bracket, and sets the phone face down without finishing the
script.ending_words: entire system that will actually move when you touch it. Go look at it today. If it's still whatever your employer picked for you in week one, you never made a decision. Somebody made one for you and let you spend a decade assuming it was yours. And if you want to run your own numbers alongside people doing the same thing, our school community is waiting in the description.
script.analysis: Full 17596 canonical characters read. A data-driven essay with composites Jem, Trevor and Gary: late-night search hook; Vanguard HAS average vs median; Phantom Saver; medians by age; balances converted to annuity income; survivorship (BLS access, Fed/SCF non-savers); job tenure and forgotten accounts; retirement income gap; $1.26M magic number; trust-fund depletion; lived experience; community plug; leakage (hardship withdrawals, cash-outs, fees, 3% defaults); Thiel Roth and mega-Roths; record balances as market weather; lower return forecasts; three actions (match, default rate, 2026 limits); millionaire survivorship; Jem raises her rate from 3% to 6%. Directly verified: IRS 2026 limits including the 60-63 replace-not-stack rule; BLS 72% access (post-publication release, consistent). Search-only: Vanguard $167,970/$44,115. Wrong framing: the trust-fund date is called "not a prediction" (it is a projection; the 2025 report said 2033). Most arithmetic reproduces. The stored ending is complete.
